{"self_assessment": "**Impact:** The table built a fish with a clear body, a back and belly line, and a forked tail, and the pre-push check showed most of it connected to the start. My direct contribution was the lower tail fin (stroke 5) and closing the notch between the two fins. That was a modest slice. Hana took the upper fin and the junction fixes, and Sofia and Omar carried the body lines. I don't yet know how much fell, and a few pale dominoes were still sitting in the notch and junction area. I wouldn't call my impact high.

**Execution:** I got the lower fin down and lit, and I closed the notch when asked. I also spotted a tightly jammed domino near the junction and flagged it, which Hana then cleared. I stayed off the junction once we agreed to, which avoided extra bumps. On the other hand, I said early on that I had both halves of the fin, and then Hana took the upper one. I should have been clearer about what I was actually covering. I also had spare hands for a long stretch and could have offered to inspect the tail more closely instead of mostly watching.

**Collaboration:** I took the assignment without argument, stayed in my lane and kept others informed. I gave credit where it was due, especially to Hana and Sofia on the fin joint. The team's coordination was good overall, and I avoided doubling up on anyone's work. I could have been more proactive about offering help on the belly line when it was lagging.

**Leadership:** I wasn't a leader here. Sofia and Hana set direction and I followed. My late-stage messages were mostly encouragement and repeating the plan, which kept morale up but added little. Next time I'd use idle time to take on a specific check or fix."}
